races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Sam Davis III
cands.bio: Elizabeth City real estate broker who owns a brokerage. He has served on the Pasquotank County Board of Commissioners on and off for many years, holding an at-large seat during his 2026 campaign. He was a district director for the county commissioners' association. Democrat who won North Carolina House District 5.
cands.gaps: We found no statements from Sam Davis III on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or other issues. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and no campaign site or interview was available. We found no documented actions in his county commissioner service on these issues. We found no controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements. His exact birth year (1951 or 1952) and the dates of his commissioner terms are not established. His birthplace and upbringing rest on a single Wikipedia description.

cands.name: Bill Ward
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 5 since January 2023. U.S. Army veteran who worked in law enforcement for 33 years. Born in Elizabeth City, NC. Lost his 2026 re-election bid to Democrat Sam Davis III.

endorsements.text: Listed in 'tommy's Picks' (Sway voting group by tommy aycock) for 2026, per Ballotpedia.

In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he named these endorsers (self-reported): Southern States Police Benevolent Association, NC Values, NC State Optometric Society, Grass Roots NC, Human Coalition, and the NC Home Builders Association, among others.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Bill Ward was raised, when he lived in North Carolina as an adult, or where he worked in law enforcement. Ballotpedia names Central High School but not its location. We found no documented position of his on data centers or on development and growth. We found no stated position on homestead property taxes or on abortion. The pages did not show any bill he sponsored, and we could not verify specific actions in office for the issues in this guide. His statements about laws he helped pass come from his own survey answers and were not checked against official records. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey.

qual.why: Two terms of legislative service plus a long public-safety career put him near the top of the middle band. The pages show no law, policy or budget career, and committee roles are not counted.

workers-first.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he helped pass laws requiring North Carolina sheriffs to cooperate with ICE in identifying and removing criminal illegal aliens.

land-for-floridians.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he helped pass laws restricting land purchases in North Carolina by adversarial governments and protecting military installations.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site describes him as 'Pro Second Amendment' and ties that to his law enforcement career.

back-police-order.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said police, fire and EMS must be funded at an appropriate level, opposed defunding police and bail reform, and called for court reform so criminals are appropriately punished.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said parents should help decide whether children attend public, charter or private schools.
